issue: Audit fix X10 renamed VERTEX_PASS to VERTEX_TINT. The rename is sound, since "pass" is reserved vocabulary, but it overrides the binding decision D14 (m3_decisions.md:47: `VERTEX_DIFFUSE = 0, VERTEX_PASS = 1, VERTEX_END = 2`) without amending it. The T3.11 card (lines 30, 79, 82, 83, 88) still specifies VERTEX_PASS and `{PASS, …}`. Decisions, card and code now disagree on the name of one concept.

votes.reason: The facts in the finding are mostly accurate, but it does not describe a real problem in the project. (1) `m3_decisions.md` and `m3_sweep.md` are not project files. `git ls-files` has no match and `git log --all` has no history for them. They exist only in the session scratchpad (/tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/m3_decisions.md). They are working notes for one round of card fixes. Their own header says the names are binding only "so all editors use the same words" in that round, and the edit they called for is already in the card (`PainterlyPathVertexKind`). Amending D14 would change no repo artifact, and no later agent reads that file: per docs/tasks/README.md, "A card is the agent's whole mandate". (2) The card and code differ on purpose, and the audit already records it. docs/audits/TQ.1.md:93 states the rename and says "The T3.11 card's interface block still shows the old name (historical record, not edited)". That is the "note it in the review log" fix the finding proposes, and the commit message dff970a also records "VERTEX_PASS -> VERTEX_TINT". (3) Leaving the card alone was correct under CLAUDE.md rule 1. The TQ.1 card's scope is `src/**`, analysis, tools, tests, Makefile and CMakeLists.txt, and `docs/tasks/` is not in it. (4) Nothing downstream is stale. Across the tracked tree, VERTEX_PASS appears only in the completed T3.11 card (line 30, plus the `{PASS,…}` pseudo-code at lines 79–88) and in the audit row that documents the rename. No later card (T3.13–T3.18, M4, M5), docs/architecture.md or any test uses it. path.h is not a CONTRACT file. So no current or future mandate gives an agent conflicting names.

The rename and the stale card text are real, but the finding's main claim does not hold up.

1. "D14" is not a project decision. `m3_decisions.md` and `m3_sweep.md` are in the session scratchpad, not the repo. `git ls-files` lists neither, and `git grep m3_decisions|m3_sweep|D14` finds nothing in the repo (the only hit is pixel bytes in a .ppm). The file calls its names "binding, so all editors use the same words" for one finished card-fix sweep. D14 itself was about adding the `Painterly` prefix (m3_sweep.md item 1.2 renamed `PathVertexKind` to `PainterlyPathVertexKind`), not about choosing "PASS". So nothing in the project "overrides a binding decision without amending it". The proposed fix of amending D14 means editing a throwaway orchestration note.

2. The card drift is already recorded and was done on purpose. `docs/tasks/M3/T3.11-integrator-path.md` does still say `VERTEX_PASS` (line 30) and `{PASS, ...}` (lines 79, 82, 83 and 91; the finding's "88" is wrong). But the audit row X10 (`docs/audits/TQ.1.md:93`) says "The T3.11 card's interface block still shows the old name (historical record, not edited)". The TQ.1 card's Scope is `src/**`, `analysis/**`, `tools/**`, `tests/**`, `Makefile` and `CMakeLists.txt`, with output only to `docs/audits/TQ.1.md`. Under CLAUDE.md rule 1 the auditor was not allowed to edit the T3.11 card, so recording the drift in the audit was the correct action.

3. Recording it in the review log is one of the remedies the finding itself offers, and the audit already does that.

4. Nothing else depends on the old name. `VERTEX_TINT` is used only in `src/painterly/kernel/integrator/path.h`. T3.12 and later cards and code refer only to the `PainterlyPathVertex` struct, and `src/test/test_path.cpp` uses only `VERTEX_END`. T3.11 is a finished card, so no future work will read it and get the wrong name.

issue: The film layout of 3 channels per pixel is defined in the integrator layer (PAINTERLY_CHANNELS, used for the offset at path_trace.cpp:40), while the kernel's painterly_film_accumulate hard-codes channels [0], [1] and [2]. This is the same kernel-versus-integrator split that F7 flags for the miss object id, but the audit does not list it.

votes.reason:
The facts in the finding are right, but they are not the problem it describes. buffers.h:15 does define PAINTERLY_CHANNELS = 3. path_trace.cpp:40 and :76 use it, and write.h:17-19 index [0], [1], [2]. docs/audits/TQ.1.md does not list this. Neither file has changed since the audit (the last commit to touch buffers.h is e5e46b7).

The analogy to F7 does not hold:
1. **F7 is one value defined twice, which must stay equal.** The kernel returns the literal `-1` (kernel/integrator/path.h:179). The integrator then defines PAINTERLY_OBJECT_ID_MISS = -1 "as painterly_primary_object_id returns it", and buffers.cpp:20 fills object_id with it. Change either one alone and the two layers disagree.
2. **The film case has no shared value.** The kernel never uses a channel count or a stride. `painterly_film_accumulate(double *pixel_sum_rgb, double3 L)` writes the three components of a double3 at the pointer it is given. The width is set by the double3 type and stated in the name `pixel_sum_rgb`.
3. **The stride belongs to the host.** Only path_trace.cpp (host integrator) uses the stride, to compute the offset and to check buffer sizes. Any PAINTERLY_CHANNELS >= 3 still works with the kernel (for example 4 for RGBA). Nothing has to be kept equal across the two layers.
4. **This matches upstream Cycles.** The project mirrors Cycles. In the pinned upstream .cache/vendor/blender-v5.2.2/intern/cycles/kernel/film/write.h:128-134, `film_overwrite_pass_float3` writes `buffer[0] = value.x; buffer[1] = value.y; buffer[2] = value.z;` with no shared constant. `film_write_pass_float3` (:68-76) uses `buffer + 0/1/2` the same way. In Cycles the pass stride is computed on the host. Painterly's write.h is the same pattern.

The proposed fix would move a host buffer-layout constant into the kernel film header. That is the reverse of the Cycles design and adds no safety: the kernel has nothing to check against it except, at most, a static_assert. Leaving it out of the audit is not a defect.

The quoted lines are accurate at HEAD (6abe417). buffers.h:15 defines `PAINTERLY_CHANNELS = 3`. write.h:17-19 writes `pixel_sum_rgb[0..2]` from `L.x/.y/.z`. path_trace.cpp:40 and :76 and buffers.cpp:18 use the constant. docs/audits/TQ.1.md has no entry for it.

It is still not a real defect, and it is not the same split as F7.

1. **No value is written twice.** In F7 the miss sentinel `-1` is a literal in the kernel (path.h) and also a named constant in the integrator, so the same meaning has two definitions. Here the kernel never handles the per-pixel stride. `painterly_film_accumulate(double *pixel_sum_rgb, double3 L)` gets a pointer to one pixel's triple and adds the three components of a `double3` into it. The `[0]/[1]/[2]` are the component offsets of a 3-vector, set by the `double3` type itself. They are not a copy of a channel count. The stride (`PAINTERLY_CHANNELS * pixel`) and the buffer size are computed only in the integrator.

2. **This is the upstream Cycles pattern the project mirrors.** In the pinned checkout, `.cache/vendor/blender-v5.2.2/intern/cycles/kernel/film/write.h:68-78`, `film_write_pass_float3` writes `buffer + 0`, `+ 1`, `+ 2` from `value.x/.y/.z`. The pass layout and stride stay outside that function. CLAUDE.md asks for Cycles naming and layout.

3. **The architecture doc puts the layout in the integrator on purpose.** docs/architecture.md:61 says `PainterlyRenderBuffers` lives in `painterly/integrator/buffers.h`, next to `PainterlyPathTrace`, which fills it.

4. **The proposed fix changes nothing in the kernel.** Moving `PAINTERLY_CHANNELS` into kernel/film/write.h would leave the kernel body the same: it would still write `.x/.y/.z`. F7's fix, by contrast, replaces a kernel literal. The constant would just sit in another file, and that breaks with the documented placement and the Cycles precedent.

At most this is a matter of taste, not a missing audit item.

issue: The thread code (the shim `thread` builds a std::thread on glibc and calls pthread_create on macOS/musl; PainterlyThreadPool sits on top of it) is linked to no thread library. The repo's own oracle links Threads::Threads. On glibc < 2.34, such as the manylinux_2_28 wheel image (glibc 2.28), pthread_create/pthread_join live in libpthread.so.0. libstdc++'s std::thread then emits strong references to them, so an executable fails to link, and the module gets unversioned imports that the symbol audit rejects. This is latent today because no wheel binary links the thread code yet. It becomes live when T3.15 links the engine into _painterly.

votes.reason:
The failure the finding describes does not happen. Every binary that links the thread code, now or as planned, already gets libpthread through Embree. Embree's common/sys/CMakeLists.txt:4-5,23 runs FIND_PACKAGE(Threads REQUIRED) and then TARGET_LINK_LIBRARIES(sys ${CMAKE_THREAD_LIBS_INIT} ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS}). `sys` is a static library, so this dependency passes as LINK_ONLY to everything that links painterly::embree. On this host (glibc 2.39, CMAKE_HAVE_LIBC_PTHREAD=1) the variable is empty, which is why only `-ldl` shows up today.

To check the glibc < 2.34 case, I configured a scratch build with -DCMAKE_HAVE_LIBC_PTHREAD=0, the result FindThreads gets on manylinux_2_28. FindThreads then found pthread_create in libpthread, and the generated build.ninja links both targets in question with -lpthread:
- `_painterly`: `... libcycles_util.a ... libsys.a -lpthread -ldl ...`
- `painterly_tests`: `... libsys.a -lpthread -ldl ... libpainterly_util.a libcycles_util.a`

Both reach Embree through existing links. _painterly links painterly::embree directly (src/blender/CMakeLists.txt). painterly_tests links painterly_integrator, which links painterly_bvh, which links painterly::embree. In both, Embree's own sys objects reference pthread_create, so libpthread is recorded as DT_NEEDED and later references resolve against it.

So no executable fails to link, and the module gets no unversioned pthread imports. T3.15 links painterly_session into _painterly, and that chain also pulls in Embree, so the change it plans does not expose the problem either.

The suggested explicit Threads::Threads link on cycles_util would only be a robustness tweak. No current or planned target builds the thread code without Embree.

The finding is literally true that cycles_util and painterly_util declare no Threads::Threads, but the failure it predicts does not happen, now or in T3.15. Every binary that links the thread code also links Embree. Embree's own build adds the thread library: common/sys/CMakeLists.txt:5 runs FIND_PACKAGE(Threads REQUIRED), and :23 runs TARGET_LINK_LIBRARIES(sys ${CMAKE_THREAD_LIBS_INIT} ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS}). kernels/CMakeLists.txt:349 links sys PRIVATE into the static embree, which CMake passes on to consumers as LINK_ONLY. Embree needs this itself, because its libsys.a has strong undefined pthread_create and pthread_join (checked with nm on build/dev/_deps/embree-build/libsys.a). _painterly links painterly::embree directly (src/blender/CMakeLists.txt:12). painterly_tests gets Embree through painterly_bvh (PRIVATE painterly::embree on a static library) and painterly_integrator. I checked this with a scratch configure that mimics glibc 2.28 (-DCMAKE_HAVE_LIBC_PTHREAD=0, Embree and doctest sources taken from build/dev/_deps). FindThreads then gives -lpthread, and build.ninja puts -lpthread (after libsys.a) on the link line of both _painterly and painterly_tests. libsys.a's own pthread references make libpthread.so.0 a DT_NEEDED entry even under --as-needed, so references from cycles_util and painterly_util bind to its versioned symbols. That means no link failure and no unversioned imports for the symbol audit. T3.15 (docs/tasks/M3/T3.15-bindings.md:32) only adds painterly_session etc. to _painterly. _painterly keeps painterly::embree, and the session layer reaches Embree through painterly_bvh, so the scenario never becomes live. The suggested explicit Threads::Threads link would be hygiene at most, not a fix for a real defect.
